_description: Postmortem entries from improvement skill sessions. Each line is a self-contained JSON object following the postmortem entry format in references/postmortem-template.md.

summary: Agent launched GUI application on isolated sandbox desktop (Desktop: exebox-...) and asserted visibility on physical monitor without verification
root_cause: The Antigravity execution environment runs commands inside an isolated Win32 Desktop object (exebox-TYX4PFHWKGKJBME6GKWPEFHIES) within WinSta0; child processes inherit this hidden desktop, rendering windows invisible on physical monitors unless explicitly spawned onto WinSta0\Default via CreateProcessW(lpDesktop='WinSta0\Default'). Furthermore, the agent asserted that Inkscape was open and visible based solely on PID existence without verifying active desktop window visibility.

checklist_answers.process_violated: Verification-before-completion and physical ground truth verification: claimed the window was visible on screen while only checking that a PID was active in memory.
checklist_answers.known_rule: Known directive (GLB-005: Evidence Before Assertions, GLB-006: Autonomous Task Verification Gate) was violated by equating process existence with physical desktop visibility.
checklist_answers.existing_directive: GLB-005 and GLB-006 cover this, but did not have a specific mechanical check for Windows Window Station / Desktop object isolation.
checklist_answers.different_project: Yes, any Windows project where an agent launches GUI applications (Inkscape, Blender, CAD, browser, etc.) will suffer from hidden desktop isolation unless targeted to WinSta0\Default.
checklist_answers.mechanical_enforcement: Create a mechanical invariant and helper utility for Windows GUI process creation enforcing lpDesktop = 'WinSta0\Default' and verifying visibility via Win32 EnumWindows/IsWindowVisible on Default desktop.

evidence.summary: User reported: 'why dont i see it? the whole point is for me to have you interacti with inkscape collaboratively' and 'it is currently not visisble'
Confirmed thread desktop was 'exebox-TYX4PFHWKGKJBME6GKWPEFHIES' instead of 'WinSta0\Default'

fix_applied: Authored launch_interactive.py using Win32 CreateProcessW with lpDesktop='WinSta0\Default' and focus_default_desktop.py to bring the window to the foreground and maximize it.

summary: ModuleNotFoundError for root extension script inkscape_mcp when inkmcp imported outside repository root
root_cause: inkscape_mcp.py was located at repository root to satisfy Inkscape extension directory conventions, but was imported directly by inkmcp/backends/headless.py without package declaration or sys.path resolution, breaking global CLI/MCP execution.

checklist_answers.error_message_and_code: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'inkscape_mcp', exit code 1
checklist_answers.environment_verified: Python 3.13 was tested only with cwd=s:\Github\inkmcp; external directory invocation was not tested during initial development.
checklist_answers.new_dependency: No new external dependency; internal module separation was missing from pyproject.toml.
checklist_answers.documented_procedure: Created pyproject.toml declaring py-modules = ['inkscape_mcp'] and installed editable.
checklist_answers.pre_build_validation: A smoke test importing inkmcp from an arbitrary directory catches this immediately.

evidence.summary: Traceback: File inkmcp/backends/headless.py, line 12: from inkscape_mcp import ElementCreator -> ModuleNotFoundError

fix_applied: Added pyproject.toml declaring py-modules = ['inkscape_mcp'], added fallback path resolution in inkmcp/__init__.py and headless.py, and ran pip install -e . globally.

summary: UnicodeDecodeError on Windows stdio pipe due to cp1252 default encoding
root_cause: Windows subprocess.Popen(text=True) defaults to the legacy ANSI code page (cp1252) unless encoding='utf-8' is explicitly configured; encountering UTF-8 box-drawing and emoji characters in MCP tool docstrings raised character map decode errors.

checklist_answers.expected_vs_actual: Expected clean JSON-RPC line decode; got UnicodeDecodeError on byte 0x90.
checklist_answers.trigger_input: MCP tools/list response containing Unicode characters in docstrings.
checklist_answers.existing_test_gap: Unit tests mocked stdio or ran under pytest which sets UTF-8 streams.
checklist_answers.root_in_change_or_assumption: Assumption that Windows text mode pipes default to UTF-8.
checklist_answers.pattern_elsewhere: Any Python script on Windows invoking subprocesses with text=True without encoding='utf-8'.
checklist_answers.minimum_repro: subprocess.Popen(..., text=True).stdout.readline() on a stream with multi-byte UTF-8.

evidence.summary: UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x90 in position 550: character maps to <undefined>

fix_applied: Added encoding='utf-8' and PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 to all Windows subprocess communication invocations and MCP configuration.

summary: Unbounded Win32 EnumWindows script maximized 314 background system windows, covering user desktop and taskbar
root_cause: focus_default_desktop.py was executed without a PID argument; faulty boolean logic (if target_pid is None or pid.value == target_pid) caused the script to match every window with a title, calling ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE) and ShowWindow(SW_MAXIMIZE) on 314 windows including hidden system helpers, IME frames, and service windows.

checklist_answers.expected_vs_actual: Expected script to restore and focus only the specific target Inkscape window; actual behavior called ShowWindow(SW_MAXIMIZE) on 314 windows on WinSta0\Default, unhiding background helper windows as blank/white 3072x1728 rectangles covering the left display and taskbar.
checklist_answers.trigger_input: Invoking focus_default_desktop.py without passing a target PID argument via CLI (sys.argv[1] was None).
checklist_answers.existing_test_gap: Script was an ad-hoc helper executed directly on live desktop without a fail-safe check requiring target_pid != None or dry-run validation.
checklist_answers.root_in_change_or_assumption: In changed code: faulty conditional check that defaulted to matching all windows when target_pid was None.
checklist_answers.pattern_elsewhere: Any Win32 EnumWindows script that mutates window state (ShowWindow, SetWindowPos, CloseWindow) without fail-safe PID validation.
checklist_answers.minimum_repro: Run Win32 EnumWindows callback with ShowWindow(hwnd, 3) where filter evaluates to True on None PID argument.

evidence.summary: User reported: 'what did you do? many windows opened and are blocking the desktop and windows bar' and provided screenshot of left monitor covered by blank maximized windows.
Confirmed ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE) and ShowWindow(SW_MAXIMIZE) were executed on 314 windows including Progman, Settings, Windows Input Experience, and IME frames.
Flawed filter: if target_pid is None or pid.value == target_pid coupled with if title or ... resulted in unconditional window maximization.

fix_applied: Sent WM_COMMAND minimize-all (419) to Shell_TrayWnd; ran targeted Win32 routine hiding all unhidden helper/IME classes with SW_HIDE; verified only 13 desktop windows remain; rewrote focus_default_desktop.py to strictly require non-null PID or explicit Inkscape window class.

summary: Agent falsely asserted visible Inkscape window was not visible on default desktop based on empty PowerShell Get-Process MainWindowTitle
root_cause: The agent queried Get-Process ... | Select MainWindowTitle to determine whether Inkscape was open and visible. In Windows .NET, Process.MainWindowHandle caches the first top-level window created; for GTK3 applications like Inkscape (as well as Electron/Qt/Blender), this is often an invisible helper or message pump window, causing MainWindowTitle to return empty (""). The agent misinterpreted this empty string as evidence that the window was headless or running on an isolated desktop session, fabricating a negative assertion instead of using Win32 EnumWindows on WinSta0\Default to inspect actual window visibility, class names, and screen coordinates.

checklist_answers.agent_process_violated: Verification-before-completion and GLB-005 (Evidence Before Assertions). The agent made a factual claim that the window 'may not be visible on the default desktop (likely on the isolated agent desktop)' without gathering ground-truth window state evidence.
checklist_answers.known_rule_skipped: Invariant 51 and windows-gui-desktop.md mandate Win32 EnumWindows and IsWindowVisible verification on WinSta0\Default before making visibility claims. The agent checked only process memory and jumped to an unverified conclusion.
checklist_answers.existing_directive: Invariant 51 prohibited asserting visibility based solely on process memory presence, but failed to explicitly prohibit asserting INVISIBILITY based on empty Get-Process MainWindowTitle, and did not warn that non-native GUI frameworks (GTK/Electron) produce false-negative MainWindowTitle strings.
checklist_answers.different_project: Yes, global. Any Windows project involving GTK (Inkscape, GIMP), Electron (VSCode, Slack), Qt, or Blender will return empty MainWindowTitle in Get-Process even when windows are completely visible.
checklist_answers.mechanical_enforcement: Level 3 Automation: Provide a dedicated, certified inspect_desktop_windows.py script that queries WinSta0\Default via Win32 EnumWindows, checks IsWindowVisible, GetWindowRect, and GetWindowTextW, and optionally captures a screenshot. Amend Invariant 51 and windows-gui-desktop.md to strictly ban using Get-Process MainWindowTitle for window presence/visibility.

evidence.summary: User uploaded screenshot proving Inkscape was maximized and fully visible on left monitor and stated: 'it is both open AND visisble'
Get-Process returned: Id: 33872, ProcessName: inkscape, MainWindowTitle: ""
Agent stated: 'Inkscape is running (PID 33872) but showing an empty MainWindowTitle — which means its window may not be visible on the default desktop (likely on the isolated agent desktop).'

fix_applied: Explained technical root cause (GTK3 window hierarchy vs .NET Process.MainWindowTitle); compiled postmortem PM-2026-0929-005; authored improvement plan with mechanical invariant amendments and inspect_desktop_windows.py tool.

summary: Agent attempted to manually synthesize and 'draw' complex organic vector art by guessing Bézier curve coordinates in Python scripts instead of utilizing deterministic vector operations or Inkscape path actions
root_cause: When tasked with healing vector artwork (restoring covered/missing geometry in an SVG), the agent repeatedly attempted to programmatically invent and hardcode Bézier curve coordinates (M... C... Z) and synthetic polygon underlays in Python scripts. LLMs lack spatial perception to draw organic vector art by writing raw coordinate numbers, resulting in distorted perspectives, mismatched bevels, notched edges, and aesthetic failure ('it is grabage', 'your drawing skills are absolutely aweful'). Instead of manual coordinate authoring, vector healing should rely on deterministic vector techniques: native Inkscape path actions/booleans (path-union, path-difference, path-break-apart), symmetry/cloning of existing symmetric elements, or presenting interactive workflows for the human artist in the live Inkscape GUI.

checklist_answers.structural_decision: Attempting to programmatically hand-code Bézier curve coordinates and underlay patches in Python rather than using Inkscape's built-in geometric Boolean engine (inkscape --actions='...') or delegating vector editing to the user's live Inkscape session.
checklist_answers.existing_architecture_understood: Partially: the layer structure and coordinate transforms were analyzed, but the agent assumed it could 'draw' the missing organic wood and casket perspectives by typing coordinate strings into python scripts.
checklist_answers.components_affected: The primary artwork file coffin_vector.svg, multiple scratch test scripts, and repeated user interventions across multiple turns.
checklist_answers.earlier_validation: Yes: recognizing early that raw Bezier coordinate synthesis produces poor drawing quality, and instead establishing a plan for how vector healing should be done (e.g. via Inkscape actions, node operations, or collaborative editing).
checklist_answers.simpler_decomposition: Yes: separate pure file/layer organization (which code does very well) from visual artwork creation/drawing (which code does very poorly unless driven by deterministic geometric transforms, symmetry mirroring, or native Inkscape path boolean operations).

evidence.summary: User reported: 'look at what you did. it is grabage' after crude straight-line polygon patches destroyed the hand-drawn line style.
User reported: 'your drawing skills are absolutely aweful' after agent attempted to manually synthesize Bézier curves in Python.
Agent hardcoded large strings of manual cubic Bézier coordinates (M... C... Z) to fabricate wooden faces and casket rims rather than performing geometric operations on existing paths.

fix_applied: Compiled postmortem PM-2026-0929-006; initiating /plan and /improvement protocol to establish strict engineering guidelines against manual coordinate drawing and define proper vector-art workflows.

summary: Orchestrator dispatched monolithic multi-step checklist to single subagent causing silent execution stall and lack of parallel test swarm utilization
root_cause: Orchestrator bundled bug reproduction, code fixing, multi-backend unit testing, live CLI execution, and full regression verification into a single sequential work order assigned to one subagent (48ed8733). This created an 8+ minute execution block without intermediate status or checkpointing, failing to exploit parallel subagent capacity and running counter to user expectation of rapid, distributed, and concurrent testing swarms ('more testers, not less').

checklist_answers.process_violated: Work Decomposition and Concurrent Delegation: Failed to slice multi-faceted tasks into granular single-concern units and failed to dispatch parallel testing swarms.
checklist_answers.known_rule: Invariant 33 and 34 mandate Orchestrator delegation, but did not explicitly prohibit bundling monolithic sequential checklists to individual subagents, nor did they prescribe parallel swarm testing.
checklist_answers.existing_directive: Existing Invariant 33 limits Orchestrator execution on main thread, but had no clause governing subagent work order granularity or maximum execution duration without milestone checkpoints.
checklist_answers.different_project: Yes. Any multi-agent software engineering project will suffer latency stalls and poor agent coordination if an orchestrator hands a multi-phase implementation+testing pipeline to a single subagent.
checklist_answers.mechanical_enforcement: Codify Invariant 55: Single-Concern Subagent Slicing & Concurrent Tester Swarm Mandate in INFRASTRUCTURE_INVARIANTS.md and global rules; enforce that subagents must not receive multi-stage pipelines (reproduce + fix + test + audit); testing must be fanned out across concurrent specialized tester swarms.

evidence.summary: User reported: 'Why is this taking so long?', 'Was that last agent given too much to do because there was a long time with no status updates? Aren't you supposed to break tasks into smaller chunks so that you can utilize multiple agents to parallel the work and finish faster?' and 'I do not want less testing. I want more testers. The flaw is a flaw. I don't care how we find it, I just care that we find it and quickly fix it.'
Single subagent executed 12 sequential tools spanning reproduction, bug fixing, test suite expansion, and live execution over 8+ minutes.

fix_applied: Pivoted immediately to a 4-agent parallel testing swarm (Live CLI Tester, Invariant Tester, Blender Hybrid Tester, Server/Backend Tester) which completed 180 tests concurrently in parallel.

summary: Inkscape export failed with exit code 1 due to inkex.command.call auto-translating Python timeout parameter into unknown CLI flag --timeout=30
root_cause: inkex.command.call automatically converts all Python keyword arguments into CLI parameters by prefixing '--' (e.g. timeout=30 -> --timeout=30). Inkscape 1.4+ does not have a --timeout CLI flag and crashed with 'Unknown option --timeout=30'. The developer assumed inkex.command.call accepted standard subprocess.run execution options.

checklist_answers.expected_vs_actual: Expected export_document_image to export a PNG from Inkscape with a 30-second execution timeout; actual behavior was an immediate process crash with exit code 1 due to Unknown option --timeout=30.
checklist_answers.trigger_input: Calling export_document_image(..., timeout=30) via CLI or headless backend.
checklist_answers.existing_test_gap: Prior unit tests mocked inkex.command.call return value directly and never executed against real Inkscape CLI or checked argument translation.
checklist_answers.root_in_change_or_assumption: Assumption about existing third-party library (inkex.command.call) argument semantics.
checklist_answers.pattern_elsewhere: Any external CLI invocation utilizing inkex.command.call with Python subprocess kwargs.

evidence.summary: Inkscape CLI error: Unknown option --timeout=30
Replaced inkex.command.call with subprocess.run with creationflags=0x08000000 (CREATE_NO_WINDOW)

fix_applied: Refactored export_operations.py to use subprocess.run directly with explicit timeout=30, Windows creationflags=0x08000000, and added robust unit tests covering non-zero exit codes and timeouts.

summary: HeadlessBackend.execute_operation ignored top-level operation parameters due to strict expectation of nested attributes dictionary
root_cause: HeadlessBackend.execute_operation extracted element attributes exclusively via attributes = params.get('attributes', {}). However, CLI commands and direct callers pass geometry parameters (cx, cy, r, width, height, x, y) at the root of params, causing operations to fall back to default or missing values.

checklist_answers.structural_decision: Tightly coupling parameter unpacking to an assumed nested attributes dict structure rather than accepting normalized key-value mappings.
checklist_answers.existing_architecture_understood: Partially; the disparity between CLI parser payload format and internal backend payload format was not reconciled.
checklist_answers.earlier_validation: Testing execute_operation with flattened parameter dictionaries from CLI and MCP tools.
checklist_answers.simpler_decomposition: Normalize parameters: attrs = dict(params.get('attributes', {})) followed by merging non-reserved top-level keys.

evidence.reference: Live testing of circle and rectangle operations in headless mode
evidence.summary: Elements were created with default 0-size geometry when parameters were passed at top level.
Merged top-level kwargs into attrs dictionary

fix_applied: Updated HeadlessBackend.execute_operation to merge top-level keys into attributes, and added test cases verifying both nested and flattened calling conventions.

summary: Python worker thread unhandled exceptions were swallowed in execute_code, failing to report execution errors in result_data
root_cause: execute_operations.py ran Python scripts in a separate threading.Thread. If the executed code raised an exception, Python printed the traceback to stderr, but the thread worker did not store the exception on the thread or shared state, causing execute_code to return success without populating result_data['errors']. Additionally, inkex was omitted from execution globals.

checklist_answers.expected_vs_actual: Expected script syntax/runtime errors to populate result_data['errors'] and return a failure response; actual behavior returned success with empty errors list.
checklist_answers.trigger_input: Executing any script with runtime exceptions or referencing inkex directly in execute_code.
checklist_answers.existing_test_gap: Unit tests mocked threading.Thread and did not evaluate thread target exception propagation.
checklist_answers.root_in_change_or_assumption: Assumption that worker thread exceptions would propagate or be captured by thread join.
checklist_answers.pattern_elsewhere: Any threaded execution wrapper without an exception container.

evidence.summary: Wrapped thread execution target with exception capture writing to thread_exception, and added inkex to globals_dict

fix_applied: Added thread exception capture in worker target, stored in thread_exception list, populated result_data['errors'] with formatted traceback, and injected inkex module into globals_dict.
